transcript.text:
Here are the most common causes, roughly in order from easiest to hardest to check:

## 1. Power supply
• Check the breaker or fuse box. Look for a tripped breaker labeled "dishwasher" or "kitchen."
• Check the GFCI outlet. Some dishwashers plug into an outlet under the sink, or a nearby outlet with "Test/Reset" buttons. Press Reset.
• Check the wall switch. Many kitchens have a switch near the sink (often next to the garbage disposal switch) that powers the dishwasher. It may have been flipped off by accident.
• Check the plug. If it plugs in under the sink, make sure it hasn't worked loose.

## 2. Door not latching
• Dishwashers won't start unless the door is fully closed and latched. Push it firmly shut.
• Check that dishes, utensils, or a rack aren't sticking out and blocking it.
• If the latch feels loose or doesn't click, the door latch/switch may be faulty, which is a common repair.

## 3. Control settings
• Child lock / control lock: Many models have this. Look for a lock icon. It's usually disabled by holding a button (often "Heated Dry," "Lock," or "Start") for 3–5 seconds. Check your manual for your model.
• Delay start: Make sure a delayed start hasn't been set.
• Reset the control board: Turn off the breaker for 1–5 minutes, then turn it back on.

## 4. Other possibilities
• Blown thermal fuse (no lights or response at all)
• Faulty control board or touchpad
• Bad door switch
• Water supply issue (if it powers on but doesn't fill)

## To help narrow it down:
• Are there any lights or display at all, or is it completely dead?
• Does it beep or show an error code?
• What's the brand (Bosch, Whirlpool, Samsung, LG, etc.)?

Let me know and I can give more specific steps.
Totally dead, no lights or display, no beeps. It's a Neff, 6 years old. Was fine yesterday.

Since it's completely dead, start with power. Neff (made by BSH, same as Bosch and Siemens) usually fails this way for one of a few reasons.

## Quick checks first

1. Are you looking in the right place?
On most integrated Neff models the controls are on the top edge of the door, and the display only shows when the door is open. Open the door, press the On/Off button firmly (some models need a 1–2 second hold), then close it.

2. The fused spur switch
Most UK dishwashers run off a switched fused spur, a wall switch, often above the worktop near the sink, sometimes labelled "dishwasher."
• Check it's switched on.
• It has a small fuse holder on the front. The fuse (usually 13A) can blow without tripping anything else. Swap it for a known-good one if you can.

3. The plug fuse
If it plugs into a socket in an adjacent cupboard, check the plug is fully in, and swap the 13A fuse in the plug for one from another appliance you know works (e.g. a kettle).

4. The socket itself
Plug something else (a phone charger or lamp) into the same socket to confirm it's live.

5. Consumer unit (fuse box)
Look for a tripped MCB or RCD. If the RCD keeps tripping when the dishwasher is connected, stop there. That points to an electrical fault in the machine.

6. Hard reset
Switch off at the spur/breaker for 5 minutes, then back on.

## If power is definitely reaching it

These are the usual culprits on a 6-year-old Neff:
• Control/power module: the most common cause of a totally dead BSH dishwasher. It's a replaceable board, usually £100–200 for the part.
• Door wiring harness: on models with controls in the door, the cables run through the hinge and can fray or break from years of opening and closing. It's cheaper to fix and worth checking.
• Mains cable or connection block: less common, but possible.

These involve removing panels, so unplug or isolate it fully first. If you're not comfortable with that, it's a job for an engineer.

## Worth checking
• Whether you bought an extended warranty or home appliance cover.
• Neff's own repair service, or a local independent engineer, who is often cheaper.

Did the fuse swaps or socket test turn anything up?
Spur switch is on and the neon light is lit. Other sockets work and nothing's tripped at the fuse box. Don't know how to check the fuse in the spur and I've no spare. Door's closed and latched fine.

The neon being lit is good news. On most fused spurs the neon sits after the fuse, so if it's glowing, the fuse is almost certainly fine and power is reaching the outlet.

## Two quick things before assuming a fault

1. Try it with the door open.
On most Neff integrated models the buttons and display are on the top edge of the door and only work or light up when the door is open. Open it, press and hold the On/Off button for 1–2 seconds, and look at the top edge for any light. If nothing at all, carry on below.

2. Check how it's connected.
Look in the cupboard next to it or under the sink:
• If it plugs into a socket, there's a second fuse in the plug. Swap it with the fuse from your kettle's plug (unscrew the plug or prise out the fuse carrier). Also try plugging the dishwasher into a different socket if the cable reaches.
• If the cable goes straight into the wall or spur (no plug), it's hardwired, and there's nothing more to check on the supply side.

## Checking the spur fuse anyway (optional)
Switch the spur off. The small rectangular cover on the front is the fuse carrier. Prise it out with a flat screwdriver, and the fuse clips inside. You can test it by swapping in the 13A fuse from your kettle plug. But with the neon lit, this is unlikely to be the problem.

## If it's still dead
Power is reaching the machine, so the fault is inside it. On a 6-year-old Neff, the likely causes are:
• Power/control module: the most common cause of a completely dead BSH dishwasher
• Door wiring harness: wires through the hinge can break from wear, which is cheaper to fix
• Mains cable or terminal block: less common

These need the machine pulled out and panels removed, so it's usually a job for an engineer unless you're confident with appliance repairs. Isolate it at the spur first if you do look yourself.

## Before calling someone, check:
• Neff's own service (often a fixed-price repair) vs. a local independent engineer, which is often cheaper
• Home insurance or extended warranty, since some policies cover appliance breakdown
• Repair vs. replace: if quoted much over £200, a new machine may be better value at 6 years old

If you let me know whether it plugs in or is hardwired, and the model number (inside the door edge), I can narrow it down further.
Model on the door edge is S513G60X0G. I can't see a plug and I can't pull the machine out, so I don't know if it's hardwired. Still no display at all.

That model is a fully integrated Neff, so the controls and display are on the top edge of the door. If you've had the door open, pressed On/Off and seen nothing at all, it's genuinely dead rather than a display quirk.

## Finding the connection without pulling it out

The plug is usually in the cupboard next to it, most often under the sink:
• Look at the back wall of the cupboard for a socket, possibly hidden behind pipes, bins or bottles.
• Look for a grey or white cable coming through a hole in the cupboard side. That'll be the dishwasher's power lead (and you'll usually see the water hoses nearby).

Also look at the spur switch itself:
• If a cable comes straight out of the bottom or front of the faceplate, the dishwasher is wired directly into the spur, with no plug.
• If not, the spur feeds a hidden socket somewhere, usually under the sink.

## Make sure the spur is actually for the dishwasher
Kitchens often have several spurs (washing machine, fridge, boiler). Switch it off and see if anything else stops (fridge light, washing machine display). If something else goes off, you may have been checking the wrong switch.

## One last reset
Switch the spur off for 10 minutes, back on, then open the door and hold On/Off for 3 seconds.

## If it's still dead
Power is reaching it and nothing's tripping, so it's almost certainly an internal fault. On this type of Neff, the usual suspects are:
• Power/control module: the most common cause of a totally dead machine
• Door wiring harness: on fully integrated models, wires run through the hinge into the door controls and can break after years of opening and closing. This is a cheaper fix.

Both need the machine pulled out and the door panels removed, so with it stuck in place, this is a job for an engineer.

## Getting it fixed
• Neff (BSH) service: book online with the model number. They usually offer a fixed-price repair covering parts and labour.
• Independent engineer: often cheaper for a module or harness fault.
• Cover: check your home insurance, any appliance cover, and whether you bought an extended warranty. Some Neff models came with extended guarantees, so dig out the paperwork.

A repair typically costs much less than replacing an integrated dishwasher (which also means refitting the door panel), so on a 6-year-old Neff, it's usually worth repairing.
